analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md, adding head lines 956-991 that describe a startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The supplied units are BASE text at lines 1629-2248, which surrounds but does not include the added section. The patch excerpt is truncated at the end of the hunk, so the tail of the new text is not visible. Within the visible excerpt, the change is documentation only. It describes a warmup that runs greedy 128-token probes and shape cells under a 20-second wall budget, using the artifact's default sampling. It states that no probe or cell trains a rate or counter. There is no code, wire, key, attestation, authorization, or storage change, so no regression against the threat-model assets or boundaries (A-001, TB-007, T-041, T-029) can be identified.

Open questions for integration, which are outside the supplied evidence: (1) whether the warmup uses synthetic prompts only. Any use of real consumer content, or of the SSD prefix cache (T-041), would need review. If warmup prompts were donated to the encrypted SSD prefix cache or shared a cacheSalt, they could affect the TTFT timing oracle (SEC-035) or at-rest artifacts. The visible text does not say so. (2) whether the warmup interacts with foreground request priority and with the availability/idle-GPU behavior (T-029, T-010). The text says preemption leaves the attempt due, which suggests foreground yield, but the implementing code is not supplied. (3) whether the report link (docs/reports/2026-10-21-...) exists. This is a doc matter, not security. No findings; a low residual uncertainty remains because of the truncated patch and the absence of the implementing source.
